about: The layers of AnyTune and what each may depend on. Checked by tools/architecture/check.ts (npm run test:architecture). A file of src/ belongs to exactly one layer; a relative import must land in the same layer or in one the layer may import; a bare module specifier must be allowed for the layer; the globals a layer may not name are listed. Dependency direction: components -> app -> domain <- fusion -> audio -> domain, adapters -> domain; the harness is the only code that sees everything, and the only TypeScript that may import Vue — except its native harness (Phase 6), which mounts the same UI on OBIX's native runtime and may never import Vue.

layers.name: domain
layers.why: the musical tuning domain: pure, framework-neutral, testable without a browser, Vue, Polycall or a microphone

layers.name: music
layers.why: the music model: MIDI files, tempo maps and timelines, references, chords, tunings and the guitar fretboard — pure, framework-neutral, with no microphone, subprocess, Polycall or DOM

layers.name: instruments
layers.why: instrument tunings as data, typed by the domain

layers.name: audio
layers.why: pitch providers (simulated, recorded, later a microphone): the only layer that may reach audio input — never the DOM

layers.name: fusion
layers.why: implementations of the domain's PitchFusionPort, composed over pitch providers; no DOM, no UI

layers.name: adapters
layers.why: readers and writers of file formats AnyTune keeps compatible with (the .obr journal), implemented here — never a component, never the DOM

layers.name: polycall-node
layers.why: a Node transport of polycall_rpc v1 (TCP to a loopback Polycall runtime), for AnyTune's tools and import worker; never in the browser bundle

layers.name: polycall
layers.why: Polycall's wire (polycall_rpc v1) and the transport port: framing and payloads only. Polycall connects components across languages and decides nothing musical

layers.name: recording
layers.why: anytune-recording/1: an independent codec (to check the recorder module) and the recorder client, which reaches the C recorder module through Polycall

layers.name: synthesis
layers.why: sound sources rendered from notes (Karplus-Strong plucked strings): reference playback that follows any tempo, and the analysis's test signals — never mistaken for a recording

layers.name: analysis
layers.why: what the sound says, uncertainly: onsets, chroma and chord candidates of a declared vocabulary (refusing what is not in it), monophonic notes — pure frame processing, no microphone, no UI

layers.name: lesson
layers.why: practice: aligning what was heard with the arrangement (pitch and timing apart), feedback in words, the lesson clock (count-in, tempo, A-B loops, latency) and step mode — pure, with no microphone, DSP or Polycall

layers.name: import
layers.why: the import's decisions: which URLs are fetched and with which arguments, the job's stages, what is done with a transcription engine's notes and how they are scored — pure; the worker (services/import-worker) runs the subprocesses

layers.name: app
layers.why: the application service and its state: framework-neutral; providers and fusion are injected, never imported

layers.name: components
layers.why: the Vue-flavoured .obix UI: reads application state, emits intents; imports only "obix" and the app's view types

layers.name: native-harness
layers.why: Phase 6: mounts the same .obix UI — lowered to canonical DOP IR — on OBIX's native runtime; it may import that runtime and never Vue (it reaches the harness only for its shared types, mount-types.ts)

layers.name: harness
layers.why: the demo execution boundary: composes the layers and mounts the UI on the official Vue runtime — the one TypeScript place that may import vue; the browser entry picks the mount (#anytune-mount: the Vue harness by default, the native harness in --mode native)
